newsitem.title: FRANCE: DASSAULT EASIER AFTER PLANE ORDER WORRIES.
newsitem.headline: DASSAULT EASIER AFTER PLANE ORDER WORRIES.

text.p: The shares of French planemaker Dassault Aviation clawed back some of their losses on Monday after falling sharply in early trade following a report that the Socialist government wanted to renegotiate a tentative order by the previous conservative government for 48 Rafale fighters.
Dassault was off 2.48 percent at 1,375 francs on 1,830 shares traded at 1014 GMT. Earlier it hit a low of 1,341 francs.
Business daily La Tribune reported that the government wanted to renegotiate the deal on a piece by piece basis and would be seeking a 10 percent reduction in the cost.
"In addition to the loss in turnover, the Dassault group could lose a window for exports," commented one analyst in a broker's note.
The contract was worth 15 billion francs to Dassault, the newspaper said. The government is seeking to reduce defence costs as part of a deficit cutting drive to qualify for European monterary union.
